title: The Day of the Perfect Half
skyStory: Exactly half the moon is lit tonight, and Aquarius is very smug about the symmetry. Half light, half dark, perfectly balanced, like a cookie split fairly between two friends who have been negotiating since lunch. The gale has calmed to a grumble. Saturn says balance is earned. The moon says balance is a mood. They agree to disagree, politely.

reading: The [[Six of Pentacles]] has the scales out today, and it is weighing one thing only: how much you give versus how much you let in. Spoiler: the scale is tipped so far toward giving that it has fallen off the table. The moon would like a word.

Today's task is lopsided on purpose. Someone will offer to help with something you could easily do alone. Say yes. Say yes even if they do it slower, differently, or with a worse playlist. Watch the scale wobble back toward the middle. Half moon, half day, half the work. The Tiger is allowed to nap in a sunbeam for exactly one half hour.
joel.mission: Accept the next offer of help you receive, however tiny, and say only 'thank you, that would be great'.
joel.omen: A shoelace coming undone exactly halfway through a walk. Pause, retie, and notice that pausing was the point.

reading: The half moon is a seesaw and you are, as usual, the person who quietly makes sure everyone gets a turn. Today the seesaw wants you to sit on it yourself. Something you have been putting second, a hobby or a nap or a book, gets moved to the front of the line.

Patience is your superpower, but it has a twin called postponement, and the two of them dress alike. At around 7:15 tonight, check which one is driving. If it is postponement, kindly ask it to move to the back seat and start the thing you love for twenty minutes. Saturn will hold your calls.
nancy.mission: Spend twenty minutes on something purely for fun, and refuse to call it productive.
nancy.omen: A seesaw or a balance scale in an unexpected place. Things are evening out in your favour.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's fire, for your own joy

together.text: Split something fairly today: the last biscuit, the good pen, the window seat. Do it with ridiculous ceremony, as if a peace treaty is being signed. Then each report who won the negotiation. Both of you will claim victory. Both of you will be right.
